acceptance: A test reproduces the current behaviour, or shows that the report is wrong.
ADR D5 states whether an override value of `default` is an explicit request or no request.
build_database_config follows that rule, and the CLI and MCP surfaces match it, with tests for each.
context: Reported, not reproduced, as a follow-up from the work that merged in #2985 (b1fb45c5d). Builder precedence tests are in `tests/unit/core/test_execution_engine_config.py`. Decide first whether `default` passed in an override counts as an explicit request (it would then conflict and raise) or means "no request" (it would then not override). Record the decision in ADR D5.
description: The Polars batch agent reported that `PlatformHookRegistry.build_database_config` lets an override value of `default` beat a non-default `execution_engine` given in options. That follows the rule "builder overrides beat options". The effect is that an explicit `default` from a higher layer silently drops a non-default engine requested at a lower layer, with no warning and no recorded conflict. Conflicting explicit values are supposed to raise (ADR D5 precedence: explicit > tuning > legacy > default).
